# 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** After all Hezekiah had so faithfully done, Sennacherib king of Assyria invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, planning to conquer them.

**2** When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and intended to attack Jerusalem,

**3** he consulted with his officials and military leaders about blocking the water from the springs outside the city, and they helped him.

**4** A large workforce assembled and blocked all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?" they said.

**5** He worked with determination, rebuilding the broken sections of the wall, raising towers on it, and constructing a second wall outside the first. He reinforced the terraces of the City of David and produced large quantities of weapons and shields.

**6** He appointed military commanders over the people and assembled them in the square at the city gate to encourage them:

**7** "Be strong and courageous! Don't be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and the vast army with him, for there is a greater power with us than with him.

**8** He has only human strength, but we have the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles." The people were encouraged by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

**9** Later, while King Sennacherib of Assyria was besieging Lachish with all his forces, he sent his officers to Jerusalem with this message for King Hezekiah of Judah and all the people of Judah in Jerusalem:

**10** "Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What are you trusting in, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?

**11** When Hezekiah says, 'The LORD our God will save us from the king of Assyria,' he is misleading you — leading you to death by famine and thirst.

**12** Didn't Hezekiah himself remove God's high places and altars, telling Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before one altar only and burn incense on it'?

**13** Don't you know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were any of the gods of those nations able to save their land from me?

**14** Which of all the gods of these nations that my ancestors destroyed was able to save his people from me? So how can your God save you from me?

**15** Don't let Hezekiah deceive or mislead you like this. Don't believe him, because no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save his people from me or my ancestors. How much less will your God save you!"

**16** Sennacherib's officers said even more against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.

**17** He also wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, "Just as the gods of the other nations did not rescue their people from me, neither will the God of Hezekiah rescue His people from me."

**18** Then they shouted in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem on the wall, trying to frighten and terrify them so they could capture the city.

**19** They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as though He were like the gods of the other peoples of the world — made by human hands.

**20** King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz cried out in prayer to heaven about this.

**21** And the LORD sent an angel who annihilated every fighting man, commander, and officer in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib withdrew to his own country in disgrace. When he entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons killed him with the sword.

**22** So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from King Sennacherib of Assyria and from all their other enemies. He took care of them on every side.

**23** Many people brought offerings to the LORD in Jerusalem and valuable gifts to King Hezekiah of Judah. From then on, he was highly regarded by all the nations.

**24** Around that time, Hezekiah became deathly ill. He prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a miraculous sign.

**25** But Hezekiah's heart was proud, and he didn't respond to the kindness shown to him. So God's wrath hung over him and over Judah and Jerusalem.

**26** Then Hezekiah repented of his pride, as did the people of Jerusalem, and the LORD's wrath did not fall on them during Hezekiah's lifetime.

**27** Hezekiah had enormous wealth and honor. He made treasuries for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuables.

**28** He also built storage facilities for grain, new wine, and olive oil, and stalls for various kinds of livestock, and pens for his flocks.

**29** He acquired many cities and vast flocks and herds, because God gave him very great wealth.

**30** It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Gihon spring and channeled the water down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did.

**31** But when envoys came from the rulers of Babylon to ask about the miraculous sign that had occurred in the land, God left him to test him and to know everything that was in his heart.

**32** The rest of the events of Hezekiah's reign, including his acts of devotion, are recorded in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

**33** Hezekiah rested with his ancestors and was buried on the hill where the royal tombs are. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him at his death. His son Manasseh succeeded him as king.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **32:7-8**: "He has only human strength, but we have the LORD our God" — Hezekiah reduces the entire Assyrian crisis to one equation: flesh vs. God. And that equation has only one answer.

- **32:21**: One verse, one angel, one night, and the greatest military power on earth is humiliated. The Chronicler doesn't linger over details. He doesn't need to. God acts, and Sennacherib goes home in disgrace.

- **32:31**: God steps back to see what Hezekiah will do on his own. The Babylonian envoy visit is a character test — and Hezekiah doesn't ace it. Even the best of us have blind spots that only emerge when God stops holding our hand.


— PNEUMA
